subject: mathematics
question_text: If the matrix with rows (x−3, 2y−8) and (z+2, 6) equals the matrix with rows (5, 2) and (−2, a−4), then find the values of x, y, z and a.

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.82 — VSAQ chapter 15 Matrices, answer 99.1, on a ★★★ SSP (Super Scoring Page). recall_prompt: Say how you would find the four unknowns from this matrix equation.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Equate corresponding elements
steps.margin_note: First mark. Two matrices are equal only when EVERY corresponding entry is equal. That turns one matrix equation into four ordinary equations.
steps.memory_tip: Two matrices are equal only when EVERY corresponding entry matches — four ordinary equations.

recall.must_convey: That equal matrices have equal corresponding entries, giving four separate equations.
accept: equal matrices means every corresponding element is equal so I get four equations
equate the corresponding entries one by one
compare each position to get four small equations
corresponding elements equate cheste four equations vasthai
match each entry with the entry in the same position

steps.why: Matrix equality is defined entry by entry — same size, same entry in every position. That definition is the whole question.
common_mistakes: Equating the matrices as though they were numbers.
Matching entries in the wrong positions.

steps.label: Solve each equation
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Four one-line solves. Watch z: z + 2 = −2 gives z = −4, not 0.
steps.memory_tip: Watch z: z + 2 = −2 gives z = −4, not 0.

recall.must_convey: That the four equations are solved to give x = 8, y = 5, z = −4 and a = 10.
accept: solve each one to get x is eight y is five z is minus four and a is ten
x equals eight, y equals five, z equals minus four, a equals ten
work out the four values from the four equations
four equations solve cheste x eight y five z minus four a ten vasthai

steps.why: Each equation involves only one unknown, so none of them needs the others. That is why this is a 2-mark question and not a simultaneous-equations one.
common_mistakes: Getting z = 0 by solving z + 2 = −2 as though it were z + 2 = 2.
